title: Joint Strike Fighter (JSF) Maintenance Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (6046, 6048, 6672, 6694), DC AVN
raw_text:
10. MOS 6035, Joint Strike Fighter (JSF) Maintenance Specialist (MGySgt to
Pvt) NMOS (6046, 6048, 6672, 6694), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Joint Strike Fighter Maintenance Specialists perform
specific support functions directly related to F-35 maintenance and the
autonomic logistics information system (ALIS). This MOS will be assigned as
an NMOS only.

    b. Prerequisites. Must be skill qualified as an Aviation Maintenance
Data Specialist (MOS 6046), Flight Equipment Technician (MOS 6048), Aviation
Supply Specialist (MOS 6672), or Aviation Logistics Information Management
System (ALIMS) Specialist (MOS 6694). Refer to MOS specific Training and
Readiness Manual.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) This MOS is to be assigned only as a necessary-PMOS to qualified
6046, 6048, 6672, and 6694 Marines who have successfully completed the
requisite training course, or the appropriate on the job training, in support
of F-35 maintenance and supply functions at the squadron level and are
designated by a squadron commanding officer.

        (2) Aviation Maintenance Data Specialist, MOS 6046, must complete the
following course and be indirect support of F-35 operations Automated
Logistics Information System (ALIS) Database Administrators/Analyst Course
(N56F2M2), Eglin AFB, FL or mobile training team.

        (3) Flight Equipment Technicians, MOS 6048, must complete the course
indicated, or its equivalent United Kingdom or Air Force course, and have
minimum 6 months MOS credibility in direct support of F-35 operations at the
squadron level, and be designated by the commanding officer. Specific tasks
for MOS credibility can be found in the MOS training and readiness manual
must complete the F-35B/C Flight Equipment Organizational Maintenance Course
(N5694Q2), Eglin AFB, FL.

        (4) Aviation Logistics Information Management System (ALIMS)
Specialist, MOS 6694, must complete the courses indicated to receive the NMOS
6035 designation. Alternate means of attaining the 6035 NMOS requires a
minimum of 12 months MOS proficiency in direct support of F-35 operations and
be designated by the commanding officer. Specific tasks for MOS proficiency
can be found in the MOS training and readiness manual:

                (a) Complete the ALIS Administrator Course CID C-531-0038
(N56F2L2).

            (b) Complete the Security Plus Certification Course (M03D3RG,
M10D3RB, or M22D3R4).


                                         3-359                       Enclosure (1)
 3138                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



            (c) Complete the Network Plus Certification Course (M03KZ7G,
M10KZ7B, or M22KZ74).

        (5) Aviation Supply Specialist, MOS 6672, must have minimum 6 months
MOS credibility in direct support of F-35 operations at the squadron level,
and be designated by the Commanding Officer. Specific tasks for MOS
credibility can be found in the MOS Training and Readiness Manual.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to (bn),
NAVMC 4790.1 for MOS 6035.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Stock Clerks and Order Fillers 43-5081 (6672).

            (2) Computer Operators 43-9011 (6046 and 6694).

            (3) Production, Planning, and Expediting Clerks 43-5061 (6046).

            (4) Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers, All Other 49-9099
(6048).

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.
common_text: The Aircraft Maintenance OccFlds includes direct and indirect support of the total airframes and power plant package of all aviation aircraft weapons systems. While there is similarity in the skills required to provide this support, the systems being supported are diverse.. The following examples are provided: direct support-repair and servicing at the organizational maintenance activity which is normally accomplished on aircraft, e.g., preflight and servicing of aircraft and their systems; indirect support-repair of components at the intermediate maintenance activity which is normally accomplished off aircraft, e.g., hydraulic actuators, servos, and accumulators, aircraft engines, and transmissions. Marines entering these fields receive MOS 6000, Basic Aircraft Maintenance Marine, and then progress through specific hard skill MOSs. After completion of formal training, Marines are qualified to maintain airframes and aircraft components. The opportunity to participate in a formal apprenticeship program leading to receipt of a Department of Labor Certification of Apprenticeship Completion maybe available in some MOSs within OccFlds 60/61/ 62. As the Marine progresses, repair and administrative requirements for multiple systems take on an equal importance until the Marine is placed in a management/supervisory position. Billets for both repair and administration are varied and extend from the squadron level to staff positions at the wing, force commander, and Headquarters U.S. Marine Corps level.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
